description: # MCDashboard plugin [![License: AGPL-3.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-AGPL--3.0-blue.svg)](https://github.com/MVdWSoftware/mcdashboard-plugin/blob/main/LICENSE) A Spigot/Paper plugin that publishes an allowlist of [PlaceholderAPI](https://www.spigotmc.org/resources/placeholderapi.6245/) values over HTTPS with a live feed, so the MCDashboard mobile app can show live server stats. Only placeholders you list in `placeholders.yml` are ever resolved, and nothing is exposed until you turn it on. - Java 17, Spigot or Paper 1.18+, PlaceholderAPI on the server (Bedrock: see below). No other runtime dependencies: the HTTP server, WebSocket and JSON are the JDK's own. - HTTPS built in (self-signed or your own certificate), pairing with one-time codes and QR maps, signed tokens, per-device revocation, rate limits. - Optional history for charts, in memory or in SQLite, MySQL/MariaDB or PostgreSQL with a SOSA/SSN schema ([docs/history.md](https://github.com/MVdWSoftware/mcdashboard-plugin/blob/main/docs/history.md)). - Optional reverse tunnel and caching proxy support ([MCDashboard-proxy](https://github.com/MVdWSoftware/mcdashboard-proxy)). ## Install 1. Install PlaceholderAPI and the expansions you need. 2. Download `MCDashboard.jar` and put it in `plugins/`, or build it yourself (below). 3. Start the server once, review `plugins/MCDashboard/config.yml` ([reference](https://github.com/MVdWSoftware/mcdashboard-plugin/blob/main/docs/configuration.md)) and `placeholders.yml`, set `server.enabled: true`. 4. The plugin serves HTTPS itself (a self-signed certificate it generates, or your own); behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy set `server.tls.mode: off`. Full guide: [docs/installation.md](https://github.com/MVdWSoftware/mcdashboard-plugin/blob/main/docs/installation.md). ## Pictures, lists and tiles Placeholders of type `IMAGE` can show a web-map picture (`map:dynmap`, `map:squaremap`, `map:pl3xmap`, `map:bluemap`, see [docs/maps.md](https://github.com/MVdWSoftware/mcdashboard-plugin/blob/main/docs/maps.md)) or an `https` URL the app loads itself (`encode: false`), `LIST` placeholders send a table such as a leaderboard, and tiles take look options (`fit`, `position`, `padding`, `smoothing`, `markerIcon`, `speed`, `background`): see [docs/placeholders.md](https://github.com/MVdWSoftware/mcdashboard-plugin/blob/main/docs/placeholders.md) and [docs/dashboards.md](https://github.com/MVdWSoftware/mcdashboard-plugin/blob/main/docs/dashboards.md). ## Configuration skills (AI agents) The plugin writes six skills to `plugins/MCDashboard/.agents/skills/` (setup, configuration, placeholders, dashboards, networks, troubleshooting): Markdown instructions an AI agent (Claude Code, OpenCode, ...) loads when it helps with this server, each ending with the matching pages on [mcdashboard.org](https://mcdashboard.org/en/docs/). They are refreshed on update; see [docs/skills.md](https://github.com/MVdWSoftware/mcdashboard-plugin/blob/main/docs/skills.md). ## Bedrock (PowerNukkitX) `MCDashboard-Nukkit.jar` is the same plugin for [PowerNukkitX](https://powernukkitx.org) 3 (Java 21), using the [PlaceholderAPI for PowerNukkitX](https://powernukkitx.org/plugins/PowerNukkitX-Bundle.PlaceholderAPI). Install both jars, then follow the steps above. Differences: [docs/bedrock.md](https://github.com/MVdWSoftware/mcdashboard-plugin/blob/main/docs/bedrock.md). ## Network (Velocity / BungeeCord) `MCDashboard-Velocity.jar` and `MCDashboard-Bungee.jar` put one dashboard on the whole network. Proxies have no PlaceholderAPI, so they publish built-in network placeholders (players online, per server online and up/down, uptime, version, the paired player's ping) and can optionally read the values of backend servers that run MCDashboard. Details and limits: [docs/proxy-platforms.md](https://github.com/MVdWSoftware/mcdashboard-plugin/blob/main/docs/proxy-platforms.md). ## Build ```sh mvn -B verify # spigot/target/MCDashboard.jar, nukkit/target/MCDashboard-Nukkit.jar, # velocity/target/MCDashboard-Velocity.jar, bungee/target/MCDashboard-Bungee.jar ``` `mvn -B verify` also runs JaCoCo: the report is in `/target/site/jacoco/index.html` and the build fails below the limits set per module (`jacoco.minimum.line` / `jacoco.minimum.branch` in each `pom.xml`; the limits only go up). `core/` is at about 98% lines / 95% branches, `proxy-common/` at about 83% / 73%; the platform modules need a running server and are covered only for their pure helpers. `core/` holds everything that does not depend on a server platform (the API, authentication, history, tunnel and dashboards; JDK only). `spigot/` and `nukkit/` are the Spigot/Paper and PowerNukkitX plugins around it; `velocity/` and `bungee/` are the proxy plugins, sharing `proxy-common/`. Each shades `core/` into its jar. ## Documentation [docs/](https://github.com/MVdWSoftware/mcdashboard-plugin/blob/main/docs/README.md) covers installation, configuration, the security model, placeholders, dashboards, history, events and the tunnel. The API is described in [openapi.yaml](https://github.com/MVdWSoftware/mcdashboard-plugin/blob/main/openapi.yaml). To contribute, read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/MVdWSoftware/mcdashboard-plugin/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md); report vulnerabilities as described in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/MVdWSoftware/mcdashboard-plugin/blob/main/SECURITY.md). ## Terms and privacy The plugin's source code is licensed under the GNU AGPL v3 ([LICENSE](https://github.com/MVdWSoftware/mcdashboard-plugin/blob/main/LICENSE)). Using the MCDashboard app and the MCDashboard licence service is governed by the [terms of service](https://mcdashboard.org/en/terms-of-service/) and the [privacy statement](https://mcdashboard.org/en/privacy-statement/). Error reports are **opt-in** (`diagnostics.error-reports`, default `false`). When enabled, only an unexpected plugin error (an uncaught exception or a failed start) is sent to MVdW's own error tracker, with the exception and its stack; placeholder values, player names and server addresses are never included, and a placeholder that does not resolve is not reported. The Spigot/Paper, BungeeCord/Waterfall and Velocity jars report **anonymous usage metrics** through [bStats](https://bstats.org) (ids `35535`, `35536` and `35537`): server and player counts, software and Java version, OS and country, and whether the web server, a licence, the tunnel and which history backend are on. No server name, address, licence id, player name or placeholder value is sent. Nukkit does not report (bStats has no adapter). Turn it off in `plugins/BStats/config.yml` (`enabled: false`; `config.txt` on Velocity). ## Placeholder catalog `placeholders.yml` lists what the app may read. Entries take an optional `group` (default `General`) and `description`, and the types `AUTO` (number, boolean or text decided per value) and `IMAGE`. A top-level `catalog:` list adds every placeholder of a PlaceholderAPI expansion as an AUTO entry (`_`, parameterised ones skipped, names with `ip`, `password`, `token`, `secret` or `address` always denied, optional `params: [a, b]` to name placeholders explicitly (many expansions declare none; discovery then falls back to PlaceholderAPI's cloud data, and a warning tells you to use `params` when both are empty), `deny` globs and `max` per entry). It is read on the first server tick after startup; explicit entries win. IMAGE entries use `source: file:` (inside `plugins/MCDashboard/images/`) or `source: url:
